rates-transport-failure.reason: Adopt for #215, part of #149, by the repository owner's direction for #215, which allows pinned crates.io dependencies in bench-tools from 2026-10-19, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the program name rates.py. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: rates.py fetched with urllib and printed its URLError or HTTPError text; bench-tools rates check fetched http and https pages with curl and printed curl's error, 'rates.py: curl: (7) Failed to connect ...' for this case, as rates-decisions.v2.json decided. New behavior: bench-tools fetches them with the ureq crate over rustls. An operating-system error prints as urllib prints it, 'rates.py: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' here on Linux, so this case matches rates.py again; the errno is the platform's, so the case compares the prefix through '[Errno ' and the differential compares the whole line. A final status outside 2xx prints 'HTTP Error <code>: <reason>' as urllib's HTTPError does, but with the standard reason phrase for the code, where urllib printed the server's own phrase. A timeout prints '<urlopen error timed out>'. A TLS, name-resolution or protocol failure prints '<urlopen error <ureq's text>>', where urllib printed OpenSSL's or getaddrinfo's text and curl its own. Every one exits 2 and writes nothing, as before. As with curl, the 20-second limit covers the whole request, where urllib applied it to each socket operation, and redirects are followed. Certificates are checked against the Mozilla roots that the webpki-roots crate bundles, not the system trust store that urllib and curl read, so a page whose chain ends at a root installed only on the host fails as a TLS failure. ureq takes one proxy for every URL, the first set of ALL_PROXY, all_proxy, HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY and http_proxy, reaches http and https pages alike through it with CONNECT, and skips it for hosts NO_PROXY or no_proxy names under ureq's patterns. Built without its socks-proxy feature, ureq still takes a socks, socks4, socks4a, socks5 or socks5h URL in ALL_PROXY or all_proxy as that proxy, so it reads no HTTPS_PROXY or HTTP_PROXY, and then uses no proxy: for socks, socks4 and socks5 it connects straight to the page's host, and for socks4a and socks5h, which leave name resolution to the proxy, it prints '<urlopen error Connection refused>' without connecting. urllib chose the proxy by the URL's scheme, http_proxy or https_proxy with the lower-case name first, ignored ALL_PROXY, sent http requests to the proxy in absolute form and matched no_proxy its own way; curl also chose by scheme. So a host that sets only HTTP_PROXY now sends https sources through that proxy, where urllib and curl connected directly, one that sets an http ALL_PROXY uses it where urllib did not, and one that sets a SOCKS ALL_PROXY beside https_proxy fetches https sources without a proxy, where urllib and curl used https_proxy. Rationale: a pinned crate replaces the curl subprocess, so the command no longer needs curl on PATH and no curl configuration file can change what it does or writes. Compatibility impact: no caller parses this text; outside the Rust port and saved research, no tracked file contains 'urlopen error' or 'curl: ('. The default sources are public https pages that chain to Mozilla roots, and bun run rates:check read both on 2026-10-19 with the result rates.py printed. GitHub's runners set no proxy variables. tests/rates_http.rs pins an HTTP error status, a followed redirect, a TLS failure, an https source tunneled through HTTP_PROXY, a socks5 ALL_PROXY that shadows HTTPS_PROXY and connects directly, and a socks5h ALL_PROXY that fails without connecting, which a corpus case cannot serve or set. Resolving issue: #215.
